findings.original_finding: `accept()` does avoidable work on every call and every record. It rebuilds and serializes both RootSchemas on each call (line 318). It clones `definitions` once per table (line 333). It calls `emit::field_table(...)`, which allocates a `Vec<FieldMeta>`, inside the per-record loop (line 342). It clones each record `Value` just to deserialize it (lines 365 and 367), though `Requirement::deserialize(record)` can work from `&Value`.
findings.original_acceptance_criterion: Compute schemas and field tables once, before the loops, or cache them in a `OnceLock`. Borrow `definitions` instead of cloning it. Deserialize from `&Value` (`T::deserialize(record)`) so no clone is needed. Take the nullable-field list once per table.

findings.original_finding: `RaptorError` is the core error type, but it has one `Io` variant. It has no stable code, no recovery guidance, and no path or operation context, because `#[from] std::io::Error` discards what was being read or written. It also does not align with the structured `raptor_schema::Error` that carries category, cause and recovery.
findings.original_acceptance_criterion: Add stable machine-readable codes and recovery text to `RaptorError`. Carry the operation and path as context on I/O failures instead of using a bare `#[from]`. Pick one JSON error envelope shared with the schema `Error`.
